summary.text: Micah Jones is the Republican nominee for the open Massachusetts 6th District seat. An Army veteran who served with the 82nd Airborne Division, including in Afghanistan, he is an attorney who has represented clients before the SEC. A former Democrat who became an independent and then a Republican, he describes himself as center-right on fiscal issues and says his campaign is built on three priorities: accountability, opportunity and security.

paragraphs.text: Served in the U.S. Army from 2011 to 2016, predominantly with the 82nd Airborne Division, including a deployment to Afghanistan from 2014 to 2015.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, San Diego, and a law degree from Northeastern University School of Law, which he says he paid for using the GI Bill.

Works as an attorney representing clients before the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, including in SEC investigations and litigation; says this role barred him from trading individual stocks and that members of Congress should be held to the same standard.
Describes himself as a former Democrat; he told Fox News he left the party around 2016, during law school, and became an independent before joining the Republican Party.

In the 2026 race he says the district's seat is open for the first time in 47 years and that he would seek to work with the administration where appropriate; he describes himself as a husband and father.
